name: Tembo
tagline: Former managed Postgres platform with workload-tuned 'Stacks'; Tembo Cloud was shut down in 2025.
description: Tembo was a managed PostgreSQL platform built around 'Stacks': preconfigured Postgres instances bundled with extensions and tuning for specific workloads such as message queues (pgmq), vector search, analytics or geospatial. It also ran Trunk, a registry for Postgres extensions, and open-sourced a Kubernetes operator. In 2025 the company pivoted to an AI coding-agent product, disabled new Tembo Cloud instances on May 5, 2025, and required paid customers to migrate off by June 27, 2025. The managed database no longer exists; existing users were directed to other managed Postgres providers. Its open-source projects, such as pgmq, live on independently.
statusNote: Tembo Cloud was sunset in 2025 (new instances disabled May 5, paid instances ended June 27) as the company pivoted to AI agents; migrate to another managed Postgres.

license.name: Proprietary (service); operator and tools were open source

pricing.notes: No longer sold; the service is shut down.

scale.notes: Was single-primary Postgres; the service no longer operates.

strengths: Pioneered workload-specific Postgres 'Stacks' with curated extensions
Seeded useful open-source projects such as pgmq and the Trunk extension registry
weaknesses: Service shut down in 2025; not available for new or existing workloads
Customers had only weeks to migrate
notIdealFor: Any new project: the service no longer exists
